reason: I want to build the pump, and heart muscle should provide the force its chambers need.
expectation: The muscle will form pumping walls around the chambers; they may still need valves and a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: Making blood would support the circuit, but I chose to start with the pump.

effect: The muscular walls provide the pressure needed to push blood, so I’ll add direction control to the pump next.
reaction: The distinction between the chamber’s shape and its muscle’s force is clear.
reason: Valves should help control the direction blood flows through the chambers.
expectation: The valves will fit into the heart chambers and help prevent blood from flowing backward; the pump may still need a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: Making blood is also needed for the circuit, but I want to finish the pump first.

effect: The valves control flow in response to pressure, and the pump still needs a rhythm.
reaction: The explanation of how the valves work made their role clear.
reason: Pacemaker cells seem useful for giving the heart a regular rhythm.
expectation: The cells will add rhythmic control to the heart, though I’m unsure whether that completes the pump.

alternatives.reason: Blood is needed for the circuit, but I want to finish the pump first.

effect: The heart now has its own repeating rhythm, completing the pump; the remaining goal is the filled returning circuit.
reaction: It was interesting that the heart starts its rhythm without a separate brain command for every beat.
reason: Plasma and red blood cells should make blood to fill the circuit.
expectation: Combining them will create blood or a blood mixture for the circuit.

alternatives.reason: Connecting vessels also advances the circuit, but I chose to make its contents first.

effect: The blood provides a liquid transport medium and red cells that carry oxygen; the circuit still needs its vessels.
reaction: The distinction between the liquid and the oxygen carriers is useful.
reason: Connecting the arteries and capillary networks is the only offered combination and should advance the circuit.
expectation: I expect a connected vessel network that can carry blood toward tissues, though it may still need veins to return it.

effect: The arteries and capillaries provide an outward route and a place for exchange with tissues; veins should complete the return route.
reaction: The explanation made clear why a route for exchange matters, not just blood flow.
reason: Adding veins is the only offered combination and should provide the return path to the heart.
expectation: I expect a connected vessel circuit with veins carrying blood back toward the heart; it may still need the blood and pump added.

effect: The veins complete a route back toward the heart; the circuit still needs blood and may need the pump connected.
reaction: The return route makes the circuit easier to picture.
reason: Adding blood is the only offered combination and should fill the vessel circuit.
expectation: I expect a blood-filled vessel circuit, though it may still need to be connected to the beating heart.

effect: The vessel circuit is filled with blood, and the new goal is to connect it to the pump.
reaction: The staged assembly makes the pump and transport route easy to distinguish.
reason: Connecting the beating heart to the blood-filled circuit is the only offered combination and addresses the new goal.
expectation: I expect the heart to drive blood through the circuit, though I don't know whether this will complete the chapter.

effect: Connecting the heart completed the circulation model and showed how the pump and returning route work together to replenish blood at tissues.
reaction: Seeing the separate parts come together was satisfying, though the final choice was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding pacemaker cells was most worthwhile because it explained how the heart starts a repeating rhythm without a separate brain command for each beat.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the circuit felt predictable after making the blood and vessels, although it helped show that the pump needs material to move.

surprise.text: I was interested that cells within the heart initiate its rhythm while the brain can adjust its activity.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the offered parts had clear roles, although several later steps were the only available combinations.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the explanation of capillary exchange made me curious how circulation connects to the working tissues built earlier.
